subject: general
question: Mukund deposited ₹57,000 in a bank. With annual compounding, how much compound interest (in ₹) will he earn in 2 years if the interest rate is 10% per annum in the first year and increases by 3% per annum in the second year?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Effective Rate Method for successive years:

Effective Rate = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂) ÷ 100

Effective Rate = 10 + 13 + (10 × 13) ÷ 100 = 24.3%

Compound Interest (CI) = 24.3% of ₹57,000

CI = (24.3 ÷ 100) × 57000 = 243 × 57 = 13851

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13851.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹57,000

Rate for 1st year (R₁) = 10% per annum

Rate for 2nd year (R₂) = 10% + 3% = 13% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R₁÷100) × (1 + R₂÷100)

Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

 
 Principal End of Year 1 End of Year 2 ₹57,000 ₹62,700 ₹70,851 
• 
• +10% +13% 
 Total CI = ₹70,851 − ₹57,000 = ₹13,851 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 57000 × (1 + 10÷100) × (1 + 13÷100)

⇒ A = 57000 × (110÷100) × (113÷100)

⇒ A = 57000 × (11÷10) × (113÷100)

⇒ A = 57 × 11 × 113

⇒ A = 627 × 113

⇒ A = ₹70,851

⇒ CI = A − P

⇒ CI = 70851 − 57000 = ₹13,851

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13851.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate Method for Successive Years

When the interest rates are different for two years (R₁ and R₂), the combined effective interest rate is given by the formula: Effective Rate = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂)÷100.

Successive Percentage Change

Compound interest is essentially successive percentage increases applied one after the other. For principal P, the total amount after 2 years simplifies to P × (100+R₁)÷100 × (100+R₂)÷100.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

Simple Interest (SI) is calculated strictly on the initial principal. Compound Interest (CI) is calculated on both the principal and the accumulated interest from the previous periods, resulting in exponential growth over time.
